newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valeo falls as analysts cut estimates.
newsitem.headline: Valeo falls as analysts cut estimates.

text.p: Shares in car parts supplier Valeo fell on Thursday after the company reported a 13 percent rise in first-half profit to 740 million francs, which was on the low end of analysts' estimates and led some to cut their forecasts.
The share was down 2.6 percent at 401.40 francs at 1240 GMT, giving back most of Wednesday's three percent rise ahead of the results issued after the market close.

Lehman Brothers cut its earnings per share forecast for the group to 19.50 francs from 21.50 for 1997 and to 23.50 francs from 25 for 1998. The brokerage considers the share overvalued and has set an objective of 350 francs.

"When controlled by Cerus, there was a significant focus on EPS and cash conservation. In the new post-Cerus environment, the focus is more on expansion and volume/revenue growth," it said in a research note. "This concern is exacerbated by in-your-face commentary regarding a new focus on large acquisitions, which may involve the issue of new equity."
Paris brokerage Oddo also lowered its EPS forecast to 23.60 francs for 1998 from 24.40 francs but left its 1997 estimate unchanged.
Some analysts expressed disappointment at the absence of margin growth.
Valeo hosted an analysts' meeting on Thursday.
Investment firm CS First Boston said Valeo's first-half net attributable income and operating income were below expectations and the margin was on target.
It said in its daily research note that it was tentatively cutting the 1997 EPS estimate to 19.5 francs from 20.5.
